summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion of Al-Wajeez, focusing on the chapter of bathing (ghusl) and the five instances in which bathing is obligatory. He provides detailed explanations of janaba (sexual impurity), covering the first two instances: sperm expulsion during wet dreams or sexual climax, and intercourse between spouses. Sh. Ali Mashhour clarifies the scholarly definitions of semen in Islamic jurisprudence, distinguishing between semen expelled during sexual climax (which obligates bathing) and other physical fluids. He explains that the bare minimum of intercourse that necessitates ghusl is the entry of the head of the penis into the vagina, regardless of whether climax occurs, and addresses common misconceptions about when repeated bathing is required.
